AI glossary

The key AI terms in plain English, each with an everyday example.

  • AGI (Artificial General Intelligence): AGI describes a hypothetical AI that can handle most intellectual tasks as well as a person or better, not just narrow specialist tasks.
  • AI Act: The AI Act is the European Union’s AI law.
  • AI Agent: An AI agent is an AI system that does more than answer: it plans and carries out steps on its own to reach a goal.
  • Alignment: Alignment is the goal of making AI systems do what people actually want while respecting human values and rules.
  • API: An API is an interface that lets programs talk to each other.
  • Attention: Attention is the mechanism a transformer uses to decide which other words matter for understanding a given word.
  • Benchmark: A benchmark is a standardised test used to compare models, for example in maths, coding or general knowledge.
  • Chain of Thought: Chain of thought means a model works through a task in intermediate steps before answering.
  • Chatbot: A chatbot is a program you talk to in natural language.
  • Computer Use: Computer use means an AI operates a computer like a person: it sees the screen, moves the mouse, clicks and types.
  • Context Window: The context window is how much text a model can take into account at once in a conversation, measured in tokens.
  • Copilot: Copilot is a common name for AI assistants that work inside a piece of software and make suggestions while you stay in control.
  • Deep Learning: Deep learning is machine learning with deep neural networks, meaning networks with many layers.
  • Deepfake: A deepfake is an AI-generated or altered image, video or audio clip that makes real people appear to say or do things that never happened.
  • Diffusion Model: A diffusion model creates images, video or audio by turning pure noise into a clear result step by step.
  • Distillation: Distillation is a method in which a small model learns from a large one by imitating its answers.
  • Embedding: An embedding is a list of numbers that captures the meaning of a piece of text, an image or a sound.
  • Few-Shot Prompting: Few-shot prompting means including a few examples of the answer you want in the prompt.
  • Fine-Tuning: Fine-tuning means training an already trained model further on a smaller, targeted dataset.
  • Foundation Model: A foundation model is a large, broadly trained model that serves as the base for many applications.
  • Generative AI: Generative AI is AI that creates new content: text, images, music, video or code.
  • GPU: A GPU is a graphics processor that runs a huge number of simple calculations at once.
  • Guardrails: Guardrails are safety rules and filters around an AI model that catch unwanted inputs or outputs, such as dangerous instructions, private data or…
  • Hallucination: A hallucination is an answer that sounds convincing but is wrong or made up.
  • Inference: Inference is using a model that has finished training: it gets an input and produces an output.
  • Jailbreak: A jailbreak is a trick that gets an AI model to ignore its own safety rules, often through role play or nested instructions.
  • Large Language Model (LLM): A large language model is an AI model trained on huge amounts of text until it can predict which word is likely to come next.
  • Machine Learning: Machine learning is the part of AI in which computers learn patterns from data instead of having every rule programmed in.
  • Model Context Protocol (MCP): The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets AI applications connect to tools and data sources in one consistent way.
  • Multimodal: A multimodal model understands or produces several kinds of content, such as text, images, audio and video, and can combine them.
  • Neural Network: A neural network is a computing model made of many connected nodes, loosely inspired by nerve cells.
  • Open Weights: Open weights means a model’s trained parameters are published for download.
  • Overfitting: Overfitting means a model has memorised its training data instead of learning the underlying patterns.
  • Parameters: Parameters are the numbers inside a model that are learned during training.
  • Prompt: A prompt is what you give an AI model: a question, an instruction, a piece of text or an image.
  • Prompt Engineering: Prompt engineering is the practice of writing and testing prompts so a model gives good results reliably.
  • Prompt Injection: Prompt injection is an attack that hides instructions inside content an AI reads, such as a web page, email or file.
  • Quantization: Quantization shrinks a model by storing its numbers with less precision.
  • Reasoning Model: A reasoning model is a language model trained to think internally for longer before it answers.
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): RAG connects a language model to a search step: before answering, the system fetches relevant passages from your own documents and hands them to the…
  • RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback): RLHF is a training step in which people rate a model’s answers and the model learns to give the preferred ones more often.
  • Synthetic Data: Synthetic data is artificially generated data, often produced by an AI, used to train other models.
  • System Prompt: The system prompt is a background instruction that sets how a model should behave for the whole conversation: its role, tone, rules and limits.
  • Temperature: Temperature is a setting that controls how random a model’s word choices are.
  • Token: A token is a chunk of text that a language model works with, often part of a word.
  • Tool Use (Function Calling): Tool use means a language model can call outside tools, such as a calculator, web search, a calendar or a database.
  • Training: Training is the phase in which a model learns from data.
  • Transformer: The transformer is the neural network design behind almost every current language model.
  • Vector Database: A vector database stores embeddings and quickly finds the entries whose meaning is closest to a query.
  • Vibe Coding: Vibe coding means building software mostly by describing it in plain language and leaving most of the code to AI.
